title: One-Dimensional Motion
learning_goal: Analyze one-dimensional motion using distance, displacement, speed, velocity, reference frames, and acceleration.

stages.title: 1. Describe motion precisely
stages.content: Distance measures the total path traveled. Displacement describes the change in position and includes direction. Speed tells how fast an object moves. Velocity tells how fast and in what direction.

stages.title: 2. Choose a reference frame
stages.content: Motion is described relative to a reference point or coordinate system. A car can be moving relative to the road while a passenger is at rest relative to the car.

stages.title: 3. Worked example
stages.content: A runner moves from x = 2 m to x = 14 m in 4 s. The displacement is Δx = 14 − 2 = 12 m. The average velocity is v = Δx/Δt = 12/4 = 3 m/s in the positive direction.

stages.title: 4. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A cart moves from x = 10 m to x = 2 m in 4 s. What is its average velocity?
stages.hint: First find displacement: final position minus initial position. Keep the sign.
stages.alternate_explanation: Picture the number line. Moving from 10 m to 2 m is motion in the negative direction, so the displacement and average velocity are negative.

stages.title: 5. Acceleration
stages.content: Acceleration is the rate at which velocity changes. An object accelerates when it speeds up, slows down, or changes direction. Average acceleration is a = Δv/Δt.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, distinguish distance from displacement, speed from velocity, identify a reference frame, calculate average velocity, and interpret positive and negative acceleration.
